faq.q: What is a Base64 data URI?
faq.a: It is the image itself written as text and prefixed with a MIME type, for example data:image/png;base64,iVBOR... Browsers can display it directly from CSS or HTML without a separate file request.

faq.q: How much bigger is the encoded string?
faq.a: About 33% larger than the binary file, because every three bytes become four characters. The tool shows both sizes so you can judge whether inlining is worth it.

faq.q: When should I avoid data URIs?
faq.a: For large images. The encoded string lives inside the HTML or CSS file and cannot be cached separately, so keep data URIs for small icons and logos.
